verses.text: David count di people wey dey with am, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over dem.

David send out di people, one third under di hand of Joab, one third under di hand of Abishai di pikin of Zeruiah, Joab brother, and one third under di hand of Ittai di Gittite. Di king talk to di people say, “I myself go surely go out with una too.”

But di people talk say, “You no go go out, because if we run away, dem no go care about us. If half of us die, dem no go care about us. But you worth ten thousand of us. So now e better say you dey ready to help us from di city.”
Di king talk to dem say, “Wetin dey good for your eyes, I go do.” Di king stand by di side of di gate, and all di people go out by hundreds and by thousands.
Di king command Joab, Abishai and Ittai, talk say, “Deal gently for my sake with di young man, Absalom.” All di people hear when di king give all di captains command about Absalom.
Di people go out into di field against Israel, and di battle happen for di forest of Ephraim.
Dere dem defeat di people of Israel before David servants, and di slaughter for dat day dey great, 20,000 men.
Di battle spread over di face of all di country, and di forest devour more people dat day pass di sword devour.

Absalom meet David servants. Absalom dey ride on im mule, and di mule go under di thick branches of one great oak, and im head catch for di oak, and e hang between heaven and di earth. Di mule wey dey under am go on.
One man see am and tell Joab, talk say, “Look, I see Absalom hang for one oak.”
Joab talk to di man wey tell am say, “Look, you see am, so why you no strike am down to di ground dere? I for give you ten shekels of silver and one belt.”

Di man talk to Joab say, “Even if I receive 1,000 shekels of silver for my hand, I no go put out my hand against di king pikin man, because for our hearing di king command you and Abishai and Ittai, talk say, ‘Make everybody beware of di young man Absalom.’
Or if I don deal falsely against im life, because nothing dey hidden from di king, you yourself go set yourself against me.”
Den Joab talk say, “I no go waste time like dis with you.” E take three spears for im hand, and thrust dem through di heart of Absalom, while e still dey alive for di middle of di oak.
Ten young men wey carry Joab armour surround Absalom, strike am and kill am.
Joab blow di trumpet, and di people return from pursuing Israel, because Joab hold di people back.
Dem take Absalom, throw am into one big pit for di forest, and pile one very great heap of stones on top am. All Israel run, every man to im tent.

Now Absalom, for im lifetime, don take and set up for imself di pillar wey dey for di King Valley, because e talk say, “I no get pikin man to keep my name in remembrance.” E call di pillar after im own name, and dem dey call am Absalom Monument to dis day.
Den Ahimaaz di pikin of Zadok talk say, “Make I run now, and carry news to di king, how di Lord don avenge am of im enemies.”
Joab talk to am say, “You no go be di bearer of news dis day, but you go carry news another day. Dis day you no go carry news, because di king pikin man don die.”
Den Joab talk to di Cushite say, “Go, tell di king wetin you don see.” Di Cushite bow to Joab, and run.

Ahimaaz di pikin of Zadok talk again to Joab say, “Wetin go happen, I dey beg you, make I also run after di Cushite.” Joab talk say, “Why you wan run, my pikin man, since you no get news wey go bring you reward?”
“Wetin go happen, I go run.” E talk to am say, “Run.” Den Ahimaaz run by di way of di plain, and pass di Cushite.
Now David dey sit between di two gates. Di watchman go up to di roof of di gate by di wall, lift up im eyes, look, and see one man dey run alone.
Di watchman shout and tell di king. Di king talk say, “If e dey alone, news dey im mouth.” E come near, closer and closer.
Di watchman see another man dey run. Di watchman call to di gatekeeper, talk say, “Look, another man dey run alone.” Di king talk say, “Dis one too dey carry news.”
Di watchman talk say, “I think say di running of di first one na like di running of Ahimaaz di pikin of Zadok.” Di king talk say, “Na good man, and e dey come with good news.”

Ahimaaz call, talk to di king say, “All dey well!” E bow down with im face to di earth before di king, talk say, “Blessed be di Lord your God, wey don deliver up di men wey lift up dem hand against my oga di king.”
Di king talk say, “Di young man Absalom dey safe?” Ahimaaz answer, “When Joab send di king servant and me your servant, I see one great tumult, but I no know wetin e be.”
Di king talk say, “Turn aside, stand here.” E turn aside, and stand.
Look, di Cushite come. Di Cushite talk say, “Good news for my oga di king, because di Lord don avenge you dis day of all dem wey rise up against you.”
Di king talk to di Cushite say, “Di young man Absalom dey safe?” Di Cushite answer, “Make di enemies of my oga di king, and all wey rise up against you to do you evil, be like dat young man.”

Di king shake, go up to di room over di gate, and weep. As e dey go, e talk say, “My pikin man Absalom, my pikin man, my pikin man Absalom! I for die instead of you, Absalom, my pikin man, my pikin man!”
Dem tell Joab, “Look, di king dey weep and mourn for Absalom.”
Di victory dat day turn to mourning for all di people, because di people hear am talk dat day say, “Di king dey grieve for im pikin man.”
Di people steal enter di city dat day, as people wey dey shame dey steal enter when dem run from battle.
Di king cover im face, and di king cry with loud voice, “My pikin man Absalom! Absalom, my pikin man, my pikin man!”

Joab come into di house to di king, talk say, “You don shame di faces of all your servants dis day, wey don save your life dis day, and di lives of your pikin man dem and your pikin woman dem, and di lives of your wives and di lives of your concubines,

because you love dem wey hate you, and you hate dem wey love you. Because you don show dis day say commanders and servants no mean anything to you. I perceive dis day say if Absalom dey alive and all of us don die dis day, den e for please you well.

Now rise, go out, and speak kindly to your servants, because I swear by di Lord, if you no go out, nobody go stay with you dis night. Dat one go worse for you pass all di evil wey don come on you from your youth until now.”
Den di king rise, and sit for di gate. Dem tell all di people say, “Look, di king dey sit for di gate.” All di people come before di king. Now Israel don run, everyone to im tent.

All di people dey argue among all di tribes of Israel, talk say, “Di king save us from di hand of our enemies, and e deliver us from di hand of di Philistines. Now e don flee out of di land from Absalom.
Absalom, wey we anoint over us, don die for battle. Now why una dey silent about bringing di king back?”

King David send to Zadok and to Abiathar di priests, talk say, “Speak to di elders of Judah, talk say, ‘Why una go be di last to bring di king back to im house, since di word of all Israel don come to di king, to im house?
You na my brothers. You na my bone and my flesh. Why una go be di last to bring back di king?’
Tell Amasa say, ‘You no be my bone and my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if you no be commander of di army before me continually in place of Joab.’”
E turn di hearts of all di men of Judah, as di heart of one man, so dat dem send to di king, talk say, “Return, you and all your servants.”
Di king return, and come to Jordan. Judah come to Gilgal, to go meet di king, to bring di king over Jordan.
Shimei di pikin of Gera, di Benjamite, wey dey Bahurim, hurry and come down with di men of Judah to meet King David.
Dere dey 1,000 men of Benjamin with am, and Ziba di servant of Saul house, and im 15 pikin man dem and 20 servants with am. Dem rush go over Jordan before di king.
Dem cross di ford to carry over di king household, and to do wetin e think good. Shimei di pikin of Gera fall down before di king, as e don cross over Jordan.
E talk to di king say, “Make my oga no count iniquity to me, nor remember wetin your servant do wrong di day wey my oga di king go out of Jerusalem, make di king no take am to heart.
Because your servant know say I don sin. Look, I don come dis day, di first of all di house of Joseph to go down to meet my oga di king.”
But Abishai di pikin of Zeruiah answer, “Dem no go put Shimei to death for dis, because e curse di Lord anointed?”

David talk say, “Wetin I get to do with una, Zeruiah pikin man dem, say una suppose be adversaries to me dis day? Dem go put any man to death dis day for Israel? Because I no know say I be king over Israel dis day?”
Di king talk to Shimei say, “You no go die.” Di king swear to am.
Mephibosheth di pikin of Saul come down to meet di king. E no dress im feet, nor trim im beard, nor wash im clothes, from di day wey di king leave until di day wey e return in peace.
When e come to Jerusalem to meet di king, di king talk to am say, “Why you no go with me, Mephibosheth?”
E answer, “My oga di king, my servant deceive me, because your servant talk say, ‘I go saddle one donkey, make I ride on am and go to di king,’ because your servant dey lame.
E don slander your servant to my oga di king, but my oga di king dey like angel of God. Do wetin dey good for your eyes.
Because all my papa house na only dead men before my oga di king, yet you put your servant among dem wey eat for your own table. So wetin right I still get to cry again to di king?”
Di king talk to am say, “Why you still dey talk of your matters? I don decide say you and Ziba go divide di land.”
Mephibosheth talk to di king say, “Make e take everything, since my oga di king don come in peace to im own house.”
Barzillai di Gileadite come down from Rogelim, and e cross over Jordan with di king, to send am on im way over Jordan.
Now Barzillai dey very old, 80 years old. E provide di king with food while e dey stay for Mahanaim, because e na very great man.
Di king talk to Barzillai say, “Come over with me, and I go feed you with me for Jerusalem.”
Barzillai talk to di king say, “How long I still go live, say I go go up with di king to Jerusalem?

I don 80 years old today. I fit know di difference between good and bad? Your servant fit taste wetin I eat or wetin I drink? I fit hear any more di voice of singing men and singing women? Why den your servant go still be burden to my oga di king?
Your servant go just go over Jordan with di king. Why di king go reward me with dis reward?

Make your servant turn back again, I dey beg you, make I die for my own city, near di grave of my papa and mama. But look, your servant Chimham dey. Make am go over with my oga di king, and do to am wetin dey good for your eyes.”
Di king answer, “Chimham go go over with me, and I go do to am wetin dey good for your eyes. Whatever you ask of me, I go do for you.”
All di people go over Jordan, and di king go over. Di king kiss Barzillai, bless am, and e return to im own place.
Di king go over to Gilgal, and Chimham go over with am. All di people of Judah, and also half of di people of Israel, bring di king over.
Look, all di men of Israel come to di king, talk to di king say, “Why our brothers di men of Judah steal you away, and bring di king and im household over Jordan, and all David men with am?”
All di men of Judah answer di men of Israel, “Because di king na our relative. Why una dey angry about dis matter? We don eat anything of di king? Or e don give us any gift?”

Di men of Israel answer di men of Judah, talk say, “We get ten parts for di king, and we get more right to David pass una. Why una despise us, say we no be di first to talk about bringing back our king?” But di words of di men of Judah dey fiercer pass di words of di men of Israel.

One wicked man dey dere, im name na Sheba di pikin of Bichri, one Benjamite. E blow di trumpet, talk say, “We no get share for David, nor inheritance for di pikin man of Jesse. Every man to im tents, Israel!”
So all di men of Israel go up from following David, and follow Sheba di pikin of Bichri. But di men of Judah stick to dem king, from Jordan even to Jerusalem.

David come to im house for Jerusalem. Di king take di ten women im concubines, wey e leave to keep di house, put dem for confinement, and provide for dem, but e no sleep with dem. So dem shut up till di day dem die, dey live as widows.
Den di king talk to Amasa say, “Call di men of Judah together to me within three days, and you dey here.”
So Amasa go to call di men of Judah together, but e stay longer pass di set time wey e appoint.
David talk to Abishai say, “Now Sheba di pikin of Bichri go do us more harm pass Absalom. Take your oga servants, and pursue am, so dat e no go find fortified cities and escape from us.”
Joab men go out after am, with di Cherethites, di Pelethites and all di mighty men. Dem go out of Jerusalem to pursue Sheba di pikin of Bichri.

When dem dey by di great stone wey dey Gibeon, Amasa come to meet dem. Joab dress for im military clothes, and over am e get belt with sword fastened for im waist for im sheath, and as e go forward e fall out.
Joab talk to Amasa say, “You dey well, my brother?” Joab take Amasa by di beard with im right hand to kiss am.

But Amasa no take care of di sword wey dey Joab hand. So e strike am with am for di belly, and spill im bowels to di ground, and no strike am again, and e die. Den Joab and Abishai im brother pursue Sheba di pikin of Bichri.
One of Joab young men stand by am, talk say, “Anybody wey favour Joab, and anybody wey dey for David, make e follow Joab.”

Amasa dey wallow for im blood for di middle of di highway. Di man see say all di people stand still, so e carry Amasa from di highway into di field, throw cloth over am when e see say everyone wey come by am stand still.
When e don remove am from di highway, all di people pass on after Joab to pursue Sheba di pikin of Bichri.
Sheba pass through all di tribes of Israel to Abel, and to Beth Maacah, and all di Berites. Dem gather together, and follow am too.
Dem come and besiege am for Abel of Beth Maacah, and dem cast up one mound against di city, and e stand against di rampart. All di people wey dey with Joab batter di wall to throw am down.
Den one wise woman cry out from di city, “Hear! Hear! I dey beg una, tell Joab, ‘Come near here, make I speak with you.’”
Joab come near am, and di woman talk say, “You na Joab?” E answer, “I be.” Den di woman talk to am say, “Hear di words of your servant.” E answer, “I dey hear.”
Den di woman talk say, “Dem dey talk before time say, ‘Dem go surely ask counsel for Abel,’ and so dem settle di matter.
We na among di peaceful and faithful for Israel. You dey seek to destroy one city, one mama for Israel. Why you go swallow up di inheritance of di Lord?”
Joab answer, “E no fit be so, e no fit be so from me, say I swallow up or destroy.

Di matter no be so. But one man of di hill country of Ephraim, Sheba di pikin of Bichri by name, don lift up im hand against di king, against David. Deliver am only, and I go depart from di city.” Di woman talk to Joab say, “Look, dem go throw im head to you over di wall.”

Den di woman go to all di people with wisdom. Dem cut off di head of Sheba di pikin of Bichri, and throw am out to Joab. E blow di trumpet, and dem disperse from di city, every man to im tent. Joab return to Jerusalem to di king.
Now Joab dey over all di army of Israel. Benaiah di pikin of Jehoiada dey over di Cherethites and di Pelethites.
Adoram dey over di forced labour. Jehoshaphat di pikin of Ahilud na di recorder.
Sheva na di scribe. Zadok and Abiathar na di priests.
Ira di Jairite too na David chief minister.
Famine dey for David days three years, year after year. David ask di Lord. Di Lord talk say, “E dey because of Saul and im bloody house, because e kill di Gibeonites.”

Di king call di Gibeonites, talk to dem. Now di Gibeonites no be of di pikin dem of Israel, but of di remnant of di Amorites. Di pikin dem of Israel don swear to dem, and Saul seek to kill dem for im zeal for di pikin dem of Israel and Judah.
David talk to di Gibeonites say, “Wetin I go do for you? Wetin I go do to make atonement, so dat una go bless di inheritance of di Lord?”

Di Gibeonites talk to am say, “E no be matter of silver or gold between us and Saul or im house. E no be our own to put any man to death for Israel.” E talk say, “Wetin una talk, na dat I go do for you.”
Dem answer di king, “Di man wey consume us, and wey plan against us so dat we no go remain for any border of Israel,
make dem deliver seven men of im pikin man dem to us, and we go hang dem up to di Lord for Gibeah of Saul, di chosen of di Lord.” Di king talk say, “I go give dem.”
But di king spare Mephibosheth, di pikin of Jonathan di pikin of Saul, because of di Lord oath wey dey between dem, between David and Jonathan di pikin of Saul.

But di king take di two pikin man dem of Rizpah di pikin woman of Aiah, wey e born to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth, and di five pikin man dem of Merab di pikin woman of Saul, wey e born to Adriel di pikin of Barzillai di Meholathite.

E deliver dem into di hand of di Gibeonites, and dem hang dem for di hill before di Lord. Di seven of dem fall together. Dem put dem to death for di first days of harvest, for di beginning of barley harvest.

Rizpah di pikin woman of Aiah take sackcloth, spread am for di rock for am, from di beginning of harvest until water pour on dem from heaven. E no allow di birds of di sky rest on dem by day, nor di animals of di field by night.
Dem tell David wetin Rizpah di pikin woman of Aiah, Saul concubine, don do.

David go and take di bones of Saul and di bones of Jonathan im pikin man from di men of Jabesh Gilead, wey steal dem from di street of Beth Shan, wia di Philistines hang dem, di day wey di Philistines strike Saul for Gilboa.
E bring up from dere di bones of Saul and di bones of Jonathan im pikin man. Dem gather di bones of dem wey dem hang.
Dem bury di bones of Saul and Jonathan im pikin man for di country of Benjamin for Zela, for di tomb of Kish im papa. Dem do all wey di king command. After dat, God listen to di prayer for di land.
Di Philistines still get war again with Israel. David go down with im servants, and dem fight against di Philistines. David faint.
Ishbibenob, wey dey among di pikin dem of di giant, wey im spear weigh 300 shekels of bronze, wey dey wear new armour, think say e go kill David.
But Abishai di pikin of Zeruiah help am, strike di Philistine and kill am. Den David men swear to am, talk say, “You no go go out with us to battle again, so dat you no go quench di lamp of Israel.”
E happen say after dis, dem get another battle with di Philistines for Gob. Den Sibbekai di Hushathite kill Saph, wey dey among di pikin dem of di giant.
Dem get another battle with di Philistines for Gob, and Elhanan di pikin of Jaareoregim, di Bethlehemite, kill Goliath di Gittite, wey im spear shaft dey like weaver beam.
Dem get another battle for Gath, wia one tall man dey, wey get six fingers for each hand and six toes for each foot, 24 in number. E too na pikin of di giant.
When e defy Israel, Jonathan di pikin of Shimei, David brother, kill am.
Dis four na pikin dem of di giant for Gath, and dem fall by di hand of David and by di hand of im servants.
David speak to di Lord di words of dis song for di day wey di Lord deliver am from di hand of all im enemies, and from di hand of Saul. E talk say,
“Di Lord na my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer, even mine;
God na my rock, I go trust am; my shield, and di horn of my salvation, my high tower, and my refuge. My saviour, you save me from violence.
I call on di Lord, wey dem suppose praise, so I don save from my enemies.
Because di waves of death surround me, di floods of wicked men make me afraid.
Di cords of Sheol surround me; di snares of death meet me.
For my distress I call on di Lord, I call to my God. E hear my voice out of im temple, and my cry come into im ears.
Den di earth shake and tremble, di foundations of heaven move and shake, because e dey angry.
Smoke go up out of im nostrils, fire from im mouth devour; coals dey burn from am.
E bow di heavens also, and come down; thick darkness dey under im feet.
E ride on one cherub, and fly; dem see am on di wings of di wind.
E make darkness round am like tents, gathering of waters, thick clouds of di skies.
From di brightness before am, coals of fire burn.
Di Lord thunder from heaven, di Most High speak with im voice.
E send out arrows, and scatter dem; lightning, and confuse dem.
Den di channels of di sea appear, di foundations of di world dey bare, at di rebuke of di Lord, at di blast of di breath of im nostrils.
E send from on high, e take me; e draw me out of plenty waters.
E deliver me from my strong enemy, from dem wey hate me, because dem too strong for me.
Dem meet me for di day of my calamity, but di Lord na my support.
E bring me out also into one large place. E deliver me, because e delight for me.
Di Lord reward me according to my righteousness, according to di cleanness of my hands e repay me.
Because I don keep di ways of di Lord, and I no depart wickedly from my God.
Because all im ordinances dey before me; as for im statutes, I no depart from dem.
I dey blameless toward am, and I keep myself from my iniquity.
So di Lord don repay me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness before im eyes.
With di merciful you show yourself merciful, with di perfect man you show yourself perfect.
With di pure you show yourself pure, with di crooked you show yourself shrewd.
You save di afflicted people, but your eyes dey on di proud to bring dem down.
Because you na my lamp, Lord. Di Lord go lighten my darkness.
Because by you I run against one troop; by my God I leap over one wall.
As for God, im way dey perfect. Di word of di Lord dey tried. E na shield to all dem wey trust am.
Because who na God, except di Lord? Who na rock, except our God?
God na my strong fortress. E make my way perfect.
E make my feet like di feet of deer, and set me for my high places.
E teach my hands to war, so tay my arms bend one bow of bronze.
You don also give me di shield of your salvation. Your gentleness make me great.
You enlarge my steps under me, and my feet no slip.
I pursue my enemies, and destroy dem. I no turn again until dem don finish.
I finish dem, and strike dem through, so dat dem no fit rise. Dem fall under my feet.
Because you don gird me with strength for battle. You don make dem wey rise against me bow under me.
You also make my enemies turn dem back to me, so dat I cut off dem wey hate me.
Dem look, but nobody dey to save dem; even to di Lord, but e no answer dem.
Den I beat dem small as di dust of di earth. I crush dem as di mire of di streets, and spread dem abroad.
You also deliver me from di strivings of my people. You keep me to be head of di nations. People wey I no know go serve me.
Foreigners go submit demselves to me. As soon as dem hear of me, dem go obey me.
Foreigners go fade away, and come trembling out of dem strongholds.
Di Lord dey alive! Blessed be my rock. Exalted be God, di rock of my salvation,
even di God wey avenge me, wey bring down di peoples under me,
wey bring me out from my enemies. You lift me up above dem wey rise up against me. You deliver me from di violent man.
So I go give thanks to you, Lord, among di nations, and go sing praises to your name.
E give great deliverance to im king, and show mercy to im anointed, to David and to im seed forever.”
Now dis na di last words of David. David di pikin of Jesse talk say, di man wey dem raise up on high talk say, di anointed of di God of Jacob, di sweet psalmist of Israel:
“Di Lord Spirit speak by me. Im word dey on my tongue.
Di God of Israel talk. Di Rock of Israel speak to me: ‘One wey rule over men righteously, wey rule for di fear of God,
e go be like di light of di morning when di sun rise, one morning wey no get clouds, like di tender grass out of di earth, through clear shining after rain.’
Surely my house no dey so with God, yet e don make with me one everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and secure. Because e na all my salvation and all my desire, although e no make am grow.
But di wicked men dey all like thorns wey dem throw away, because dem no fit take dem with hand;
but di man wey touch dem must arm imself with iron and di shaft of one spear. Dem go utterly burn with fire for dem place.”
Dis na di names of di mighty men wey David get: Josheb Basshebeth di Tahchemonite, chief of di captains. Na im na Adino di Eznite, wey lift up im spear against 800 men wey e kill at one time.
After am na Eleazar di pikin of Dodai di pikin of Ahohi, one of di three mighty men with David, when dem defy di Philistines wey gather together dere for battle, and di men of Israel don go up.
E rise, and strike di Philistines until im hand tire, and im hand cling to di sword. Di Lord work one great victory dat day. Di people return after am only to take spoil.
After am na Shammah di pikin of Agee di Hararite. Di Philistines gather together for one troop, wia dere dey one plot of ground full of lentils, and di people flee from di Philistines.
But e stand for di middle of di plot, and defend am, and kill di Philistines. Di Lord work one great victory.
Three of di 30 chief men go down, and come to David for di harvest time to di cave of Adullam. Di troop of di Philistines dey camp for di valley of Rephaim.
David dey dat time for di stronghold, and di garrison of di Philistines dey Bethlehem dat time.
David long, talk say, “Oh, make person give me drink of di water of di well of Bethlehem, wey dey by di gate!”

Di three mighty men break through di camp of di Philistines, draw water out of di well of Bethlehem wey dey by di gate, carry am, and bring am to David. But e no gree drink am, but pour am out to di Lord.
E talk say, “E no fit be so from me, Lord, say I do dis! Dis no be di blood of di men wey go put dem lives in jeopardy?” So e no gree drink am. Dis things di three mighty men do.
Abishai, di brother of Joab, di pikin of Zeruiah, na chief of di three. E lift up im spear against 300 and kill dem, and get name among di three.
E no dey most honourable of di three? So e become dem captain. However, e no reach di first three.
Benaiah di pikin of Jehoiada, di pikin of one valiant man of Kabzeel, wey do great deeds, strike two lion-like men of Moab. E go down also and kill one lion inside one pit for time of snow.
E kill one Egyptian, one impressive man. Di Egyptian get one spear for im hand, but e go down to am with one staff, snatch di spear out of di Egyptian hand, and kill am with im own spear.
Dis things Benaiah di pikin of Jehoiada do, and get name among di three mighty men.
E dey honourable pass di 30, but e no reach di first three. David set am over im guard.
Asahel di brother of Joab dey among di 30. Elhanan di pikin of Dodo of Bethlehem,
Shammah di Harodite, Elika di Harodite,
Helez di Paltite, Ira di pikin of Ikkesh di Tekoite,
Abiezer di Anathothite, Mebunnai di Hushathite,
Zalmon di Ahohite, Maharai di Netophathite,
Heleb di pikin of Baanah, one Netophathite, Ittai di pikin of Ribai of Gibeah of di pikin dem of Benjamin,
Benaiah di Pirathonite, Hiddai of di brooks of Gaash,
Abialbon di Arbathite, Azmaveth di Barhumite,
Eliahba di Shaalbonite, of di pikin man dem of Jashen, Jonathan,
Shammah di Hararite, Ahiam di pikin of Sharar di Hararite,
Eliphelet di pikin of Ahasbai, di pikin of di Maacathite, Eliam di pikin of Ahithophel di Gilonite,
Hezrai di Carmelite, Paarai di Arbite,
Igal di pikin of Nathan of Zobah, Bani di Gadite,
Zelek di Ammonite, Naharai di Beerothite, armour bearer to Joab di pikin of Zeruiah,
Ira di Ithrite, Gareb di Ithrite,
Uriah di Hittite. Dem all na 37.
Again di anger of di Lord burn against Israel, and e move David against dem, talk say, “Go, count Israel and Judah.”
Di king talk to Joab di commander of di army wey dey with am, “Go now through all di tribes of Israel, from Dan even to Beersheba, and count di people, so dat I go know di number of di people.”
Joab talk to di king say, “Make di Lord your God add to di people, 100 times as plenty as dem be, and make di eyes of my oga di king see am. But why my oga di king delight for dis thing?”
But di king word prevail against Joab and against di captains of di army. Joab and di captains of di army go out from di presence of di king to count di people of Israel.
Dem cross Jordan, and camp for Aroer, on di right side of di city wey dey for di middle of di valley of Gad, and toward Jazer.
Den dem come to Gilead, and to di land of Tahtim Hodshi. Dem come to Dan Jaan, and round to Sidon.
Dem come to di stronghold of Tyre, and to all di cities of di Hivites and of di Canaanites. Dem go out to di south of Judah, at Beersheba.
So when dem don go through all di land, dem come to Jerusalem at di end of nine months and 20 days.
Joab give di sum of di numbering of di people to di king. For Israel dere dey 800,000 valiant men wey draw sword, and di men of Judah na 500,000.

David heart strike am after e don count di people. David talk to di Lord say, “I don sin greatly for wetin I do. But now, Lord, I dey beg you, take away di iniquity of your servant, because I don do very foolishly.”
When David rise up for morning, di word of di Lord come to di prophet Gad, David seer, talk say,
“Go speak to David, ‘Di Lord talk say, I offer you three things. Choose one of dem, make I do am to you.’”

So Gad come to David, tell am, and talk to am say, “Seven years of famine go come to you for your land? Or you go flee three months before your foes while dem dey pursue you? Or three days of plague go dey for your land? Now consider, and see wetin answer I go carry back to di one wey send me.”
David talk to Gad say, “I dey in great distress. Make we fall now into di hand of di Lord, because im mercies dey great. Make I no fall into di hand of man.”
So di Lord send plague on Israel from di morning even to di appointed time. 70,000 men die of di people from Dan even to Beersheba.

When di angel stretch out im hand toward Jerusalem to destroy am, di Lord change im mind about di evil, and talk to di angel wey destroy di people, “E don enough. Now hold your hand.” Di angel of di Lord dey by di threshing floor of Araunah di Jebusite.

David speak to di Lord when e see di angel wey strike di people, talk say, “Look, I don sin, and I don do wickedly, but dis sheep, wetin dem do? Make your hand, I dey beg you, dey against me, and against my papa house.”
Gad come dat day to David, talk to am say, “Go up, set up one altar to di Lord for di threshing floor of Araunah di Jebusite.”
David go up according to di word of Gad, as di Lord command.
Araunah look out, and see di king and im servants dey come toward am. Araunah go out, and bow imself before di king with im face to di ground.
Araunah talk say, “Why my oga di king don come to im servant?” David talk say, “To buy di threshing floor from you, to build one altar to di Lord, so dat di plague go stop from di people.”
Araunah talk to David say, “Make my oga di king take and offer wetin dey good for im eyes. Look, di oxen for di burnt offering, and di threshing sledges and di yokes of di oxen for wood.
Araunah give all dis, king, to di king.” Araunah talk to di king say, “Make di Lord your God accept you.”

Di king talk to Araunah say, “No, but I go surely buy am from you for one price. I no go offer burnt offerings to di Lord my God wey cost me nothing.” So David buy di threshing floor and di oxen for 50 shekels of silver.
David build one altar to di Lord dere, and offer burnt offerings and peace offerings. So di Lord listen to di prayer for di land, and di plague stop from Israel.
